shared_elements: anthropomorphic/human form (painted stick-like figures in A; a carved human-like body with face and arms in B)
reddish-brown colouration of the imagery against a paler ground
museum display context with wall and floor visible
justification: The only real correspondence is that both surfaces carry anthropomorphic imagery in reddish-brown tones, and even that is generic. A is a long horizontal painted frieze of many small flat silhouetted figures and animals in narrative rows, while B is a single vertical carved stone body bearing a few large isolated relief motifs (discs, arcs, hands) — the medium, scale, composition and manner of rendering share nothing specific.
